speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with systemic hypertension. To begin my evaluation, have you been experiencing any headaches, vision changes, or nosebleeds recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is reassuring given his age and development; however, finding systemic hypertension in a child is unusual and suggests a secondary cause. Since he has no family history of early-onset heart disease, I need to know if you have noticed any swelling in his hands or feet, or if he has had frequent headaches despite the lack of current symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis results are normal, which helps rule out renal parenchymal disease. Since we are evaluating a 5-year-old for secondary hypertension, I need to assess for renal artery stenosis. REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound and abdominal imaging are normal, which effectively rules out renal parenchymal disease and renal artery stenosis. Given his age and the absence of renal causes, we must now evaluate for cardiac anomalies; does he have a history of cyanosis, clubbing, or a known heart murmur? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram findings show narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The echocardiogram confirms narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery, which explains the systemic hypertension and normal renal workup. I have ruled out renal causes and congenital heart defects other than this obstruction.
